question: What is the definition of personal data under the GDPR?
answer: Under the GDPR, "personal data" is defined as any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person (referred to as a "data subject"). An identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, particularly by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data, an online identifier, or to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural, or social identity of that natural person (CELEX_02016R0679-20160504_EN_TXT.pdf, p.3).

question: What is 15% of the maximum fine in euros under GDPR Article 83(5)?
answer: 15% of the maximum fine under GDPR Article 83(5), which is up to 20,000,000 EUR, is 3,000,000 EUR (CELEX_02016R0679-20160504_EN_TXT.pdf, p.72).
